summary_for_children: Al-Ikhlas says Allah is One, the Eternal Refuge, He neither has children nor was born, and nothing is like Him.
environment_concept: A quiet courtyard of geometric tiles, a shaded shelter and an open terrace facing an empty sky, where the four ayahs are read. No image, figure or symbol stands for Allah.
architecture_and_scenery: Geometric tiled courtyard, a small domed shelter with four columns, and a terrace with a low wall.

areas.name: The Reading Courtyard
areas.description: A courtyard of geometric tiles where the first ayah is read.

areas.name: Eternal Refuge
areas.description: A small shaded shelter to sit and rest in while reading 112:2.

areas.name: Nothing Like Him
areas.description: An open terrace looking out at an empty sky. Nothing is shown to stand for Allah.

activities.name: Read the four
activities.description: Put the four ayahs of Al-Ikhlas in order.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Match each place to its ayah
activities.description: Match the courtyard, the shelter and the terrace to the ayah each comes from.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Nothing compares
activities.description: Talk about why nothing in creation can be compared to Allah.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: Narration explains each ayah plainly; Allah is never depicted.

status.playable_environment: first version built: its own scene (tiled courtyard, shelter, open terrace) and two playable games
status.testing: checked in headless Chromium with software WebGL at 1280x800; not tested on phones or real GPUs
status.tested_by: automated screenshots of the scene and both games

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.tier: conceptual for the new engine (an older composed scene exists; not validated as unique)
